QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_57

question.text: In currency derivatives trading, when a trading member's collateral utilization reaches 90% of the available limit, what restriction is triggered?

answer.text: The member is placed in risk reduction mode: all unexecuted orders are cancelled, only Immediate-or-Cancel (IOC) orders are accepted, all new orders are checked for margin sufficiency, position-reducing orders are accepted and position-increasing orders are rejected if not supported by adequate margins
Trading is completely suspended for the member
New positions are allowed but at double the prescribed margin
An alert is sent but no trading restriction is imposed

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the currency derivatives workbook, when a trading member's collateral utilisation hits 90%, the member enters risk reduction mode. In this mode, unexecuted orders are cancelled, only IOC orders are permitted, every new order is checked for margin sufficiency, position-reducing orders are accepted and position-increasing orders are rejected if they are not supported by adequate margins. The Trap: The restriction is not a complete suspension, nor is it limited to plain square-off orders only — fresh IOC orders are permitted subject to margin sufficiency, and reducing orders are explicitly accepted. A "double-margin" rule or a mere alert is not the prescribed mechanism. Note: Members should track collateral utilisation in real time and act before hitting the 90% threshold, since order cancellations and IOC-only behaviour can be highly disruptive during volatile sessions.
